Show HN: Fakemetrics.com – "build in public" like a superstar
items.summary: Hi HN, I am Tigran (github.com/tigranbs) I made Fakemetrics.com as a fun experiment while testing how well Claude Opus can build pixel-identical UIs. It turned out it wasn't as easy as just prompting it, but I spent time building the system so it works almost every time. And I am pretty sure you are seeing a bunch of people posting weekend vibe-coded apps and saying "$50K/month after quitting my McDonnalds job...". Well, even my friend tried to fake it a few months back. So, I kinda did this fakemetrics.com as an experiment to see how well I can have the system that clones UIs, and packaged that as a very simple (I think) usable product for the people that want to be a superstar "build in public" type of a person with no revenue, but a perfect Stripe user growth screenshot. Useful? - Probably not that much Fun? - YES!! The best part is that Claude, ChatGPT, or Grok models aren't that good at UI clones by default, but with fakemetrics.com I kinda made a system that produces near-identical results from screenshots fairly fast. That was worth learning! Let me know what you think? Should I move on with the UI cloning as an open-source product?

items.title: Show HN: Open Academy – Math Academy-style courses for any subject
items.summary: Open Academy is an open-source app inspired by Math Academy ( https://mathacademy.com/ ). You use it to create courses on any subject, taught in a similar way. If you're unfamiliar with Math Academy, it's a maths learning site with short lessons, lots of practice questions, and reviews that bring old topics back before you forget them. I really enjoyed using it to study maths, but I couldn't find anything similar for other subjects. At the same time, I was using AI a lot to learn new topics but my lessons had no structure. So I built Open Academy to bridge that gap. You create courses with your AI of choice through the CLI, ideally grounded in your own notes or content from the web. The app handles the rest, which includes prerequisite locks, quizzes and spaced review (FSRS). I don't intend to make a managed version of this. The repo and the demo include example courses: Maths for ML, ML Foundations, Deep Learning, Transformers and LLMs, LLM Inference and Reinforcement Learning so you can get a feel fo rit. MIT licensed. Runs with Docker, on Vercel with Neon, or fork it do with it as you please as far as hosting is concerned. Demo: https://open-academy-demo.vercel.app

Show HN: Comemo – composite memory provider for Hermes Agent
items.summary: There are many memory providers that can be used externally with Hermes Agent. However, like many other AI agents, Hermes only provides one slot for an external memory provider. Comemo takes that slot and acts as a composite provider. How? It fans out memory writes to multiple backends such as Mem0, Honcho, and Supermemory. On retrieval, it queries the enabled providers, merges their results, and removes duplicates before returning them to Hermes. I intend to add support for more memory providers and eventually extend Comemo to other open-source AI agents with similar limitations.

items.title: Show HN: Canonry – how a software engineer runs a marketing agency
items.summary: Hey all, I spent 10 years as a software engineer and earlier this year I opened up a marketing agency solo. My initial motivation was exploring a new field, but the thesis developed into: as building software keeps getting faster + cheaper, marketing and distribution matter more than ever. And marketing itself is changing (AI agents recommending products). I started building Canonry to automate some of my processes with agents, and it turned into a system that now practically runs my agency day to day. For one hotel client, Google AI impressions are up 15x since August. Canonry is open source (MIT) and agent-first: CLI, MCP, API, agent skills + a full UI, backed by a single local SQLite DB with your own data and keys. I think this is where marketing teams are headed. I'd love your feedback :)
